title: Lesson 12 · Pronouns & Adjectives in Depth
blurb: Reflexive pronouns, who vs whom, degrees of comparison, kinds of definitive adjectives, and adjective mistakes.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun:

“I hurt ___.”
items.explain: The action turns back on “I” — myself.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun:

“She saw ___ in the mirror.”
items.explain: The action turns back on “She” — herself.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun:

“They helped ___.”
items.explain: The action turns back on “They” — themselves.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun:

“He blamed ___.”
items.explain: The action turns back on “He” — himself.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun:

“We enjoyed ___.”
items.explain: The action turns back on “We” — ourselves.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun (one person):

“You can do it ___.”
items.explain: One person spoken to — yourself.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun:

“The cat washed ___.”
items.explain: The action turns back on “the cat” — itself.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank with the right reflexive pronoun (more than one person):

“You all did it ___.”
items.explain: More than one person spoken to — yourselves.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“___ wrote the letter?”
items.explain: It is the subject (the doer) — Who.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“___ did you call?”
items.explain: It is the object of “call” — Whom.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“the man ___ spoke”
items.explain: It is the subject of “spoke” — who.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“the man ___ I saw”
items.explain: It is the object of “saw” — whom.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“___ is there?”
items.explain: It is the subject — Who.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“To ___ shall I give it?”
items.explain: It is the object of the preposition “To” — whom.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“the girl ___ won”
items.explain: It is the subject of “won” — who.

items.prompt:
Choose who or whom:

“___ do you trust?”
items.explain: It is the object of “trust” — Whom.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“tall”
items.explain: “tall” is the simple quality — positive.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“taller”
items.explain: “taller” compares two — comparative.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“tallest”
items.explain: “tallest” is highest among three or more — superlative.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“more useful”
items.explain: “more useful” compares two — comparative.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“best”
items.explain: “best” is highest among three or more — superlative.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“richer”
items.explain: “richer” compares two — comparative.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“happy”
items.explain: “happy” is the simple quality — positive.

items.prompt:
Which degree of comparison is this?

“most hurtful”
items.explain: “most hurtful” is highest among three or more — superlative.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“tall”
items.explain: Short word — add -er, -est: taller, tallest.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“big”
items.explain: Short word — double the g and add -er, -est: bigger, biggest.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“good”
items.explain: “good” is irregular: better, best.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“happy”
items.explain: y after a consonant → ier, iest: happier, happiest.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“careful”
items.explain: Longer word — use more, most: more careful, most careful.

items.prompt:
Which gives the correct comparative and superlative?

“bad”
items.explain: “bad” is irregular: worse, worst.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“this”
items.explain: “this” points out — demonstrative.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“each”
items.explain: “each” takes one at a time — distributive.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“some”
items.explain: “some” is vague in amount — indefinite.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“three”
items.explain: “three” counts — numeral.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“those”
items.explain: “those” points out — demonstrative.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“every”
items.explain: “every” takes one at a time — distributive.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“many”
items.explain: “many” is vague in amount — indefinite.

items.prompt:
Which kind of definitive adjective is this?

“second”
items.explain: “second” orders — a numeral (ordinal).

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“He is ___ than I.”
items.explain: Never double a comparison — just “taller.”

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“She is the ___.”
items.explain: Never double a superlative — just “kindest.”

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“Read the ___ rows.”
items.explain: Put the ordinal before the cardinal: first four.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“I don’t like ___ of shoes.”
items.explain: Match number — the singular “this” agrees with the singular noun “kind”: this kind.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“He seems ___ today.”
items.explain: Never double a comparison — just “happier.”

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“Study the ___ pages.”
items.explain: Put the limiting word before the cardinal number: last two.
